exitExample.py.name: Echo-until-exit loop
exitExample.py.description: Prompts repeatedly, exits the process on the exact exit command and otherwise echoes the entered text.

fiveTimes.py.name: Five-iteration while loop
fiveTimes.py.description: Prints a heading and five numbered name lines while incrementing a loop counter.

guessTheNumber.py.name: Six-guess number game
guessTheNumber.py.description: Selects one random integer from one through twenty and allows six integer guesses with high/low hints, then reports success or the target.

helloFunc.py.name: Repeated greeting function
helloFunc.py.description: Defines a no-argument greeting with three print calls and invokes that function three times.

helloFunc2.py.name: Greeting with a name parameter
helloFunc2.py.description: Defines a greeting function that uses its argument and calls it for two embedded sample names.

magic8Ball.py.name: Branch-based random fortune
magic8Ball.py.description: Maps integers one through nine to response strings, picks a random integer and prints the returned fortune.

printRandom.py.name: Five random integers
printRandom.py.description: Prints five independently selected random integers between one and ten.

rpsGame.py.name: Rock-paper-scissors loop
rpsGame.py.description: Validates a lowercased move or quit command, randomly chooses the computer move and accumulates wins, losses and ties until process exit.

swordfish.py.name: Classroom identity gate
swordfish.py.description: Repeats identity and fixed-password prompts with continue and break; the acknowledgement is a teaching example, not a secure login.

vampire.py.name: Ordered name and age branches
vampire.py.description: Uses fixed name and age sample values to show that the first matching condition prevents later age branches from running.

vampire2.py.name: Short if-elif-else example
vampire2.py.description: Uses another fixed name/age pair to select one of three ordered greeting messages.

yourName.py.name: Condition-controlled name prompt
yourName.py.description: Repeats while the current name differs from a fixed demonstration phrase, then prints thanks.

yourName2.py.name: Break-controlled name prompt
yourName2.py.description: Runs an unconditional loop and breaks only when input matches its fixed demonstration phrase.
